scope: Two 60-day CSZ questions on the frozen V2 recipe. (1) training volume: width 40, V2's existing 9000-update run (= 0.6007 epochs) reused as-is versus a new full-two-epoch run (29966 updates). (2) capacity: widths 40/80/160 at the common 9000-update budget, width 40 reusing the same V2 run. V2 recipe, data, splits and reference files stay untouched.

hypotheses.training_volume: V2's 0.6007-epoch run may be exposure-limited: two full epochs on the identical 60-day CSZ pool raise development RankIC by at least the pre-registered margin without breaching the long-short, turnover or worst-day guardrails.
hypotheses.capacity: Width, not exposure, may be the binding constraint: raising hidden_dim from 40 to 80/160 at the fixed 9000-update budget raises development RankIC by at least the same pre-registered margin without breaching the same guardrails.
hypotheses.shared_guardrail: A gain that only moves during-training loss while the three development months show no improvement is not evidence and exits the candidate pool.

roles: capacity arm at width 40 (9000 updates, not retrained)

frozen_recipe.note: experiment_id and hypothesis are run-identity metadata, not recipe knobs. Everything else must equal configs/model_v2_60d_csz.json item by item; scripts/verify_capacity_20261024.py checks the flattened key sets and fails on any other difference. data.cache_dir is deliberately left at V2's value so the three arms share one checksum-validated projection cache; cache entries rebuild themselves if they do not match.

reused_arm.reason: The width-40 9000-update arm and the 0.6007-epoch training-volume arm are the same executed run. Retraining would spend GPU time to reproduce an identical recipe/seed and would introduce a second, non-preregistered source of variation.

step_arithmetic.pool_source: runs/model-versions/v2-cloud-20261023/record.json sample_exposure_matching.arms.60d.pool_selected, i.e. the V2 60d run's selected training pool for train split 2023-08-01..2023-11-01 and the shared sample_times
step_arithmetic.epoch_share_note: the runner records achieved epochs as epoch_samples / pool_selected, so the 9000-update share is 288000/479432 = 0.6007108411620418. Dividing updates by updates_per_epoch instead gives 9000/14983 = 0.60068078, which understates the share: the epoch's tail batch is short (479432 = 14982*32 + 8), so 9000 updates cover 288000 samples rather than 9000*479432/14983.
step_arithmetic.tail_batch: modified_tlob/adapter.py iterates range(0, len(y), batch_size) per epoch, so the final batch of each epoch holds pool_selected - 14982*32 = 8 samples and still counts as one update; that is why two full epochs are 2*14983 = 29966 updates, not floor(2*479432/32) = 29964 or 2*14982.25 rounded down.

pool_recheck.when: immediately after each new run starts, before accepting the run
pool_recheck.method: read the run's events.jsonl event stage=training type=started and require samples == 479432
pool_recheck.secondary: read the run's events.jsonl stage=training type=epoch_completed/epoch_stopped rows: epoch 1 must stop at step 14983 and epoch 2 at 29966 for w40_full2epoch (samples_seen 479432 then 958864); the 9000-update arms must stop at step 9000 inside epoch 1 with samples_seen 288000
pool_recheck.on_mismatch: stop the run, discard it, recompute updates_per_epoch = ceil(actual_pool/32) and max_steps = full_epochs * updates_per_epoch with the same formula, record the deviation, and only then restart. No max_steps value may be chosen by any other rule.
pool_recheck.why: max_steps is what fixes the epoch share; a changed pool would silently change the exposure of both groups.

capacity_params.measuring_code: modified_tlob.model.ModifiedTLOB(hidden_dim=w, num_layers=4, seq_size=128, num_features=12, num_heads=1, is_sin_emb=True); sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
capacity_params.head_structure_change: final_layers flatten (hidden_dim//4)*(seq_size//4) and halve it by /4 until <=128, so the head is width-dependent: width 40 starts at 320 and needs 2 linear layers (320->80->1); widths 80 and 160 start at 640/1280 and need 3 linear layers (640->160->40->1 and 1280->320->80->1). Capacity therefore changes width and head depth together; it is not a clean width-only contrast, and any capacity conclusion must state that.

evaluation.window_boundary_note: The three windows are half-open prediction ranges on already-used development data. nov2023 runs past V2's validation split end (2023-11-15) into 2023-11-16..2023-11-30, so no window is a fresh holdout; the same months were scored in earlier model-version replays, which is why a pass here is a screening signal only.

tool.path_base: relative paths inside a replay plan resolve against the plan file's own directory, so a plan under configs/capacity_20261024/ needs ../../runs/... for repository artifacts

evaluation.paired_daily_series: for each arm, delta = arm minus v2_60d_csz on the same prediction keys, date by date; both versions are scored inside one replay run on identical keys, dates and labels, so no cross-run comparability assumption is needed
evaluation.primary_series: the three windows' paired daily deltas concatenated in chronological order and weighted equally per paired trading day; gate means are computed on this pooled series
evaluation.scoring_convention: local approximate jinyiquant.evaluation (gross forward label returns, no fees/slippage/execution); not the official platform score

bootstrap.method: moving consecutive-day block bootstrap of the pooled paired daily delta series
bootstrap.implementation: same estimator as scripts/replay_model_versions.py::_block_delta(block=5, draws, seed) applied to the pooled series; the replay plan's seed also seeds these draws
bootstrap.per_window_reporting: paired_summary.csv already reports per-window block-5 intervals; they are required stability evidence in the report but only the pooled interval gates a version

required_reporting: per-window and pooled mean deltas for rank_ic, long_short_return and turnover
each arm's own worst-day long_short_return (date and window)
training curve checkpoints (learning_curve.json/csv, every 500 steps) for every arm, including the reused V2 run's loss level at step 9000
executed steps, samples_seen and epoch share read back from events.jsonl for every new run

pre_registered_gates.frozen_statement: These numbers are the V2 record's pre_registered_thresholds, carried over unchanged and written before any capacity run started. No threshold, metric, window, step budget or gate orientation may change after results are seen; a later change invalidates the round.
pre_registered_gates.comparison: candidate minus v2_60d_csz, paired by trading day, pooled over the three development windows

gates.statistic: pooled mean of paired daily delta
gates.meaning: candidate RankIC must beat V2 by at least this mean margin

gates.statistic: pooled mean of paired daily delta
gates.meaning: candidate mean long-short may fall below V2 by at most this tolerance

gates.statistic: pooled mean of paired daily delta
gates.meaning: candidate mean turnover may exceed V2 by at most this tolerance

gates.statistic: minimum daily long_short_return of the candidate itself over the pooled three windows
gates.meaning: absolute floor on the candidate's worst development day, not a delta

bootstrap_gate.rule: the 5-day block bootstrap 95% interval of the pooled paired daily delta must exclude 0
bootstrap_gate.orientation: for rank_ic and long_short_return the interval must lie above 0; for turnover it must lie below 0. This orientation clause only resolves which side of zero a passing interval may sit on; it adds no new threshold.
bootstrap_gate.consistency_note: the tolerance gates already forbid the unfavourable direction, so an interval that excludes zero on the unfavourable side also fails its tolerance gate

pre_registered_gates.pass_rule: a version passes only if all four numeric gates and all three bootstrap intervals pass; one miss fails the version
pre_registered_gates.derived_absolute_bounds_for_this_round: not applicable: this round's gates are relative to the recomputed V2 column of the same replay run, so no absolute bound is fixed in advance
pre_registered_gates.exit_rule: a version whose training loss falls but whose development metrics show no improvement (pooled RankIC delta <= 0 and pooled long-short delta <= 0) exits the submission-candidate pool and is reported as a negative result; falling training loss alone is never evidence

decision_rule.selection: among versions passing every gate, submit the one with the highest pooled RankIC mean delta; if the top two are within 0.002 (the V2 tie-break band) choose the higher pooled long-short mean delta, then the smaller pooled turnover delta, then the smaller hidden_dim
decision_rule.handback: if no version passes every gate, submit no capacity version: the submission slot returns to the label branch (label-contrast) and this branch records the negative result and the reason
decision_rule.group_reporting: training volume (w40 two epochs vs V2 0.6007 epochs) and capacity (w40/80/160 at 9000 updates) are judged separately; passing in one group does not promote the other
decision_rule.no_post_hoc: the selection order and handback rule are frozen here; no metric, window or threshold may be substituted afterwards
decision_rule.no_checkpoint_selection: Every arm trains to its declared max_steps; epochs never binds at 9000 updates. learning_curve checkpoints (every 500 steps) are recorded diagnostics, and no early stopping, checkpoint picking or curve-based stopping may influence any run or selection.

config_validation.command: uv run python -m jinyiquant validate-config configs/capacity_20261024/<arm>.json
config_validation.note: the printed config_sha256 is the digest of the resolved snapshot, and load_config resolves the absolute output_root/data paths against the host root, so the locally printed value differs from the cloud-side value recorded in the run manifest. The file sha256 values in arms[].config_sha256 are platform independent.

what_it_checks: each arm config differs from configs/model_v2_60d_csz.json only on frozen_recipe.allowed_differences
frozen_recipe.declared_expectations still equal the V2 config values item by item
the gate values in this file equal the V2 record's pre_registered_thresholds
total_params and final_layers of ModifiedTLOB at widths 40/80/160 equal capacity_params (torch required; reported as skipped without torch)
field_and_param_checks.reproduce_param_counts: Python with torch: from modified_tlob.model import ModifiedTLOB; sum(p.numel() for p in ModifiedTLOB(hidden_dim=w, num_layers=4, seq_size=128, num_features=12, num_heads=1, is_sin_emb=True).parameters())

caveats: Single seed (11) per arm; the three development months are already-used development data from earlier rounds, so a pass is a screening signal, not independent confirmation.
The capacity contrast moves hidden_dim and final-head depth together (see capacity_params.head_structure_change), so width effects cannot be separated from head-capacity effects.
Local approximate metric (equal tail weights, no fees or slippage); it is not the official platform score.

The width-40 9000-update arm is reused, not retrained, so it carries V2's cloud-side data hashes and environment rather than a fresh run in this round; the replay recomputes its scores on the same keys as the new arms, which removes cross-run scoring differences but not the shared-data caveat.
The bootstrap pools blocks across window gaps as a documented approximation of the handed-down 5-day-block rule; per-window intervals are reported alongside.
final split 2024-10-08..2025-01-01 and the locked Q4 windows stay unopened; no capacity decision may read them.
